set_aside.unit: A4: Accepted decision A4 — R4. Authorization guard sequence (policy)
set_aside.subject: PLAT-REG-004 request decoding
set_aside.text: “an import or request carrying its own status or project facts is refused at decoding” does not define which fields count as “project facts”; legitimate requests themselves carry project_id.
set_aside.question: Which exact request fields are forbidden as client-supplied Registry context, and is project_id explicitly permitted?
options: Permit project_id but refuse Registry-derived fields such as status, exists, is_active, display_name, address and customer_ref.
Treat every project fact, including project_id, as forbidden.
Refuse only status fields and permit other project metadata.
set_aside.default_guess: Permit project_id and refuse every field that purports to reproduce a Registry answer.

witness.initial: An active producer has permission to import a snapshot for an active Registry project.
events: The producer submits the required snapshot publication containing project_id but no status or other Registry response fields.
outcomes: The decoder accepts project_id as the target identity and proceeds to server-side Registry validation.
The decoder treats project_id as a client-carried project fact and refuses the request before any Registry call.
witness.observer: The producer sees either normal import processing or a decoding refusal.

set_aside.unit: A7: Accepted decision A7 — R7. Supported external contract versions
set_aside.subject: INV-031 recognition decoding
set_aside.text: “a ... provider-carrying result is refused at decoding” does not define what makes a result provider-carrying or whether all unknown fields are forbidden.
set_aside.question: Which exact fields or shapes trigger the provider-carrying refusal, and must every unrecognized field be rejected rather than ignored?
options: Reject any field outside the closed recognition contract.
Reject only specifically named confidence, provider and raw-response fields.
Reject provider-specific fields only when they occur at designated paths.
set_aside.default_guess: Use a closed input schema and reject every unknown field at every level.

witness.initial: A valid confirmed recognition publication contains all required business fields.
events: An operator submits it with an additional top-level field named provider_model.
outcomes: The decoder treats the extra field as provider data and refuses the request with no writes.
The decoder ignores the unknown field, creates the expense from the accepted business projection and persists no provider data.
witness.observer: The authenticated operator sees either refusal or successful expense creation.

set_aside.unit: A9: Accepted decision A9 — R9. Money policy
set_aside.subject: aggregate completed work with no recorded progress
set_aside.text: The change says “missing data must not look like zero” and that every missing section value is None, but State 1 still requires BudgetView.completed_work_total and ProgressView.completed_work_total to be non-null Decimal sums of the non-None section values.
set_aside.question: When an active budget has sections but none has a progress record, is the aggregate completed_work_total the empty sum 0, unavailable, or represented through a not-configured component?
options: Return Decimal 0 while keeping every section value None.
Make the aggregate nullable and return None.
Mark the relevant view component not_configured so no aggregate is returned.
set_aside.default_guess: Mark progress not configured and avoid presenting an aggregate completed-work value until at least one progress record exists; the BudgetView contract would need an explicit corresponding rule.

witness.initial: A project has an active budget with positive planned work in two sections and no SectionProgress records.
events: A viewer reads the project overview.
outcomes: The overview returns a budget/progress view whose sections show None but whose completed_work_total is Decimal 0.
The overview treats completed work as unavailable or not configured and does not expose a zero total.
witness.observer: The viewer sees either a numeric zero completed-work total or an explicit absence of data.

set_aside.unit: A28: Accepted decision A28 — Clock policy (accepted Factory spec, 2026-08-09; one clock source, coordinator 2026-11-07)
set_aside.subject: CLK-002 witness binding
set_aside.text: The CLK-002 Required tests item has no [witness: ...] binding; the only witness lines that follow bind CLK-001.
set_aside.question: Which existing witness check asserts CLK-002, including exclusive host-clock access and the one elapsed-clock reading per viewer-entry request?
options: Bind CLK-002 to an existing named verification check.
Add a separate named verification check for CLK-002.
set_aside.default_guess: Add a dedicated clock-source-policy verification check and bind CLK-002 to it.

set_aside.unit: A28: Accepted decision A28 — Clock policy (accepted Factory spec, 2026-08-09; one clock source, coordinator 2026-11-07)
set_aside.subject: CLK-002 exclusive host-clock reader test
set_aside.text: The invariant covers every host wall and elapsed clock, while its source check names selected calls followed by the undefined phrase “and their variants”.
set_aside.question: What exact set of clock-reading mechanisms is forbidden outside the clock source, and what check is sufficient to demonstrate that the source is the only reader?
options: Treat only the explicitly named datetime, date and time APIs plus aliases/import variants as host clocks.
Cover every standard-library and OS-level wall or elapsed clock API, including clock_gettime and indirect wrappers.
Use runtime instrumentation or an architectural dependency rule instead of a syntactic call list.
set_aside.default_guess: Define a closed forbidden API set covering standard Python wall/monotonic clock entry points and their aliases, then enforce that only the clock backend may depend on them.

witness.initial: A module other than the clock source needs the current instant.
events: Its implementer calls time.clock_gettime(time.CLOCK_REALTIME), which is not explicitly listed in the Required tests item.
outcomes: The source check treats clock_gettime as one of “their variants” and fails.
The source check examines only the named functions and passes even though the module reads a host clock directly.
witness.observer: The verification gate and later maintainers see different answers about whether CLK-002 holds.

set_aside.unit: A32: Accepted decision A32 — Dependency pins and their vulnerability check (owner 2026-11-06: current service behaviour accepted; technical decisions delegated)
set_aside.subject: DEP-002 image-verdict binding
set_aside.text: The Required test requires a verdict “bound to that image's content id” but never defines the content id or the mechanism that proves the scanned image is the image started.
set_aside.question: What immutable image identity must the vulnerability verdict contain and the deploy step compare before starting the service?
options: A repository tag or deployment artifact identifier.
A hash of the installed-distribution inventory rather than the whole image.
set_aside.default_guess: Bind both scan and start to the same immutable OCI manifest digest.

witness.initial: Image A is built under tag portal:latest and passes the OSV check; image B is later assigned the same tag and contains a vulnerable installed distribution.
events: The deploy step starts portal:latest after the tag has moved from A to B.
outcomes: A tag-based interpretation accepts the earlier verdict and starts vulnerable image B.
An immutable-content-id interpretation detects that B was not the scanned image and refuses to start it.
witness.observer: The deployment operator and users see either a started vulnerable release or a blocked deploy.
